content: It describes how elagolix, a weak-to-moderate inducer of the hepatic enzyme CYP3A4 and a weak inhibitor of CYP2C19, affects the metabolism of other drugs, often by altering their levels through hepatic/intestinal enzyme modulation or P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter mechanisms. 1. Elagolix and CYP3A Substrates: Elagolix is a weak-to-moderate inducer of the CYP3A4 enzyme. When co-administered with drugs metabolized by CYP3A4, it may decrease their plasma levels. Monitor the levels of these drugs closely and consider increasing their doses if necessary. 2. Elagolix and Linagliptin: Elagolix increases linagliptin levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition but decreases its levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. 3. Elagolix and Liraglutide: Norethindrone acetate reduces the effects of liraglutide through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor glycemic control in diabetic patients. 4. Elagolix and Oral Contraceptives: Oral contraceptives may impair glucose tolerance, reducing the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetic drugs. Monitor diabetic patients for glycemic control. 5. Elagolix and Lomitapide: Elagolix decreases lomitapide levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 6. Elagolix and Loperamide: Elagolix increases loperamide levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Use caution and monitor for potential adverse effects. 7. Elagolix and Lopinavir: Lopinavir increases elagolix levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, while elagolix decreases lopinavir levels by inducing CYP3A4. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are necessary. Co-administration of elagolix 200 mg BID with strong CYP3A inhibitors for more than one month is not recommended. 8. Elagolix and Loratadine: Elagolix increases loratadine levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Use caution and monitor for adverse effects. 9. Elagolix and Lorlatinib: Lorlatinib decreases elagolix levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, while elagolix decreases lorlatinib levels. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 10. Elagolix and Losartan: Elagolix decreases losartan levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are recommended. 11. Elagolix and Lovastatin: Elagolix increases lovastatin levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition but decreases its levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 12. Elagolix and Lumacaftor/Ivacaftor: Lumacaftor/ivacaftor decreases elagolix levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 13. Elagolix and Lurasidone: Elagolix decreases lurasidone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are necessary. 14. Elagolix and Macimorelin: Elagolix decreases macimorelin levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 15. Elagolix and Macitentan: Elagolix decreases macitentan levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are recommended. 16. Elagolix and Maraviroc: Elagolix increases maraviroc levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition but decreases its levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 17. Elagolix and Mavacamten: Elagolix increases mavacamten levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Initiation of weak CYP2C19 inhibitors may require a reduced mavacamten dose. Monitor therapy closely. 18. Elagolix and Mifepristone: Mifepristone decreases norethindrone acetate effects through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and consider backup contraceptive methods. Mifepristone also increases elagolix levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are necessary. 19. Elagolix and Methotrexate: Elagolix increases methotrexate levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Use caution and monitor therapy. 20. Elagolix and Methsuximide: Elagolix increases methsuximide levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 21. Elagolix and Methylprednisolone: Elagolix decreases methylprednisolone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are recommended. 22. Elagolix and Midazolam: Elagolix decreases midazolam levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Consider increasing the oral midazolam dose if needed and monitor closely. 23. Elagolix and Mitomycin: Elagolix increases mitomycin levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Use caution and monitor therapy. 24. Elagolix and Modafinil: Elagolix increases modafinil levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism but decreases its levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 25. Elagolix and Montelukast: Elagolix decreases montelukast levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are necessary. 26. Elagolix and Morphine: Elagolix increases morphine levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Use caution and monitor therapy. 27. Elagolix and Naldemedine: Elagolix increases naldemedine levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition but decreases its levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 28. Elagolix and Nefazodone: Nefazodone increases elagolix levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration of elagolix 200 mg BID with strong CYP3A inhibitors for more than one month is not recommended. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are necessary. 29. Elagolix and Nelfinavir: Elagolix increases nelfinavir levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition and CYP2C19 inhibition. Nelfinavir increases elagolix levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are recommended. 30. Elagolix and Netupitant/Palonosetron: Elagolix decreases netupitant/palonosetron levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 31. Elagolix and Nevirapine: Elagolix decreases nevirapine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are necessary. 32. Elagolix and Nisoldipine: Elagolix decreases nisoldipine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are recommended. 38. Elagolix and Norethindrone: Elagolix decreases norethindrone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are necessary. 39.
